Deliberate impacts by the program on animals are intended to correct, at least in degree, adverse actions by man over the years of history.

There is no intention to alter the processes of natural selection which dictate that those species and subspecies which fail to successfully compete in their respective ecosystems ultimately pass into extinction. Man may, on one hand, be considered a natural part of those forces, but man's destructive capabilities have increased in recent times to a point they are no longer considered a natural force. Projection of recent trends in environmental indicators, of which animal species are one, indicates an environment is developing which would be a threat to the peace and well-being of man himself. One of the purposes of this program, therefore, is to slow down or eliminate entirely the effect of man himself on the rate at which species and subspecies disappear from the earth.
Impacts on animals: The impact of the program will fall on two groups of wildlife:
(1) The endangered forms that are the designated benefactors of the program.
(2) Associated species that live with, or will be replaced by the endangered forms.
Impacts on endangered species are all intended to be positive. This is a restatement of the objective of the program and the proposed legislation.

Impacts on other than endangered animals may be either positive or negative. Habitat protection for endangered animals will favor associated species.
